text:
The upcoming fixture list across Europe features several striking divergences between the model and Bet365, particularly where heavy favourites might be more vulnerable than the market implies. While the bookmaker holds a slight edge over the long run, several matches this weekend offer contrasting views that are worth a closer look.

The strongest expected value emerges in Serie A, where the model gives Cagliari a 27.5% chance to win at Lazio against Bet365's 13.3% at 7.5 odds. In Spain, the model is considerably more sceptical of Real Madrid away to Santander, pricing a home victory at 19.3% versus the bookmaker's 10.0% at odds of 10.0, alongside a 25.2% draw chance compared to Bet365's 13.3%. In the Bundesliga, the model heavily favours Mainz away at Elversberg, seeing an 80.5% winning probability at odds of 2.1, whereas Bet365 prices them at just 47.6%. Other notable disagreements include Levante at 5.25 odds against Atletico Madrid and Crystal Palace at 5.5 away to Tottenham.

In the latest played rounds, log loss—where a lower score reflects better accuracy—remained tight between the two, with Bet365 slightly ahead overall in England and Germany, while the model edged ahead in Ligue 1 and matched the bookmaker in La Liga. The model enjoyed emphatic hits in Serie A, assigning 91.5% to Inter's win at Venezia and 80.1% to Napoli's victory at Monza, generating tiny log losses of 0.089 and 0.222. It also softened the blow of Aston Villa's 2-1 upset of Manchester City by rating Villa at 28.6%, faring better than Bet365 on log loss (1.251 to 1.657). However, both were undone by Monchengladbach's shock 3-2 win at Stuttgart, and the model missed poorly in El Clasico, giving Real Madrid just a 17.0% chance before their 2-1 victory at Barcelona.
